editorial:
Seven Pounds is a heavy, emotional drama that pulls you in from the very first scene. Will Smith plays Ben Thomas, an IRS agent who seems to be on a mysterious mission to help seven strangers. As you watch, you slowly piece together why he's doing this and what he's hiding. The movie has a quiet, serious tone that keeps you guessing, and Rosario Dawson brings warmth as Emily, one of the people Ben meets along the way. It's not a light watch, but it's deeply moving.

The acting is strong across the board, especially Smith's restrained performance. The pacing is slow at times, which might test your patience, but it builds toward a powerful payoff. Some viewers may find the story a bit manipulative, but if you enjoy emotional dramas with a twist, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn Ben is actually Tim Thomas, who caused a car crash that killed seven people. To make amends, he plans to donate his organs to seven strangers. He befriends Emily, who has a weak heart, and falls in love with her. In the end, Tim kills himself using a deadly jellyfish so his organs can be donated. Emily receives his heart, and the other recipients get his other organs, completing his redemption.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional dramas with a twist.
